newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's reports record profits, sees.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's reports record profits, sees.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. Thursday reported record first-quarter profits of $344.5 million despite intense U.S. competition and a "slow start" in international markets.
The fast-food giant also predicted a record-breaking year.

McDonald's first-quarter earnings, equivalent to 49 cents a share, were up 14 percent from the $301.6 million, or 42 cents a share, the Oak Brook, Ill.-based company earned in the first quarter of 1996.
The per share earnings for the latest quarter were just under the First Call consensus analyst forecast of 50 cents a share.
Revenues from sales at all restaurants hit $7.83 billion, a 7 percent increase from $7.31 billion in the year-ago quarter.

"McDonald's global food service business delivered strong results in the first quarter," company Chairman Michael Quinlan said in a statement. "Despite the extremely competitive U.S. operating environment, we delivered impressive growth in U.S. sales and operating income, exceeding our own expectations.
"We are confident in our growth strategies and expect 1997 to be another record-breaking year," Quinlan said.

McDonald's said a 7 percent increase in U.S. sales to $3.99 billion from $3.72 billion in the 1996 quarter was significant given strong competition and one less sales day in the quarter because 1996 was a leap year.
U.S. sales benefited from marketing and promotions, including one tied to the board game Monopoly, the company said.

Outside the United States, sales rose 7 percent to $3.84 billion from $3.59 billion. The results were tempered by weaker foreign currencies, McDonald's said. If exchange rates had remained at 1996 levels, sales outside the United States would have risen 14 percent, the company said.
Weak economies abroad and severe weather in Europe also held comparable overseas sales down, McDonald's said.
James Cantalupo, president of McDonald's international operations, said, "I expect our international results to improve for the balance of the year."

McDonald's said it plans to add between 2,400 and 2,800 restaurants globally in 1997 with a greater emphasis on full-size traditional restaurants and international locations compared with 1996. More than 70 percent of 1997 openings will be outside the United States.
At the end of the first quarter, McDonald's had 21,276 restaurants, 12,104 of them in the United States. During the quarter, 254 restaurants were added, 10 domestically.
McDonald's stock slipped 25 cents to $50.125 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
